default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-958.title: Positive tape autocorrelation follow
E-958.hypothesis: When successive bar returns have recently been positively correlated the tape is trending in small steps (orders sliced by large participants); the next bar in the last bar's direction follows.

E-959.title: Cumulative wick pressure follow
E-959.hypothesis: Persistently longer lower wicks than upper wicks over a window show dips being absorbed by passive buyers; follow the side that keeps rejecting.

E-960.title: Day-open acceptance after an excursion
E-960.hypothesis: After the price strays far above (below) the day's open and then closes back under (over) it, the excursion was rejected and the other side takes control; follow the cross.

E-961.title: Volatility burst direction follow
E-961.hypothesis: A jump of short-term volatility over the hourly level marks new information or a large order arriving; the burst bar's direction tends to continue as others reprice.

E-962.title: Persistent-trend resume bar
E-962.hypothesis: When most recent bars keep making new session highs (lows), a one-bar pause that is immediately overtaken signals trend resumption by participants who missed the move.

E-963.title: Hour-open reclaim
E-963.hypothesis: Many desks mark the hourly open; a close back through it after most of the hour spent on the other side shifts the hour's balance and invites follow-through.

E-964.title: Rising-volume bar ladder follow
E-964.hypothesis: Consecutive same-colour bars each with more volume than the last show aggressive participation building rather than fading; follow it.

E-965.title: Wide-range midpoint cross follow
E-965.hypothesis: Once the session range is wider than usual for the time, the range midpoint is the balance line; a close through it shows the auction moving to the other half.

E-966.title: Outside bar with strong close
E-966.hypothesis: A bar that exceeds both extremes of the previous one and closes at one end means the opposite side was run over after being tested; follow the close.

E-967.title: Low-volume new extreme fade
E-967.hypothesis: A new short-term high (low) made on thin volume lacks real participation and is a liquidity poke; fade it back into the range.
